key_insight: Interface stability in structured gas-liquid contactors is governed by opening shape, wettability, and 3D topology, with elongated flat openings giving the best pressure margin and stiffness.
engineering_relevance: For gas diffusion electrodes, geometry can widen the safe operating window against flooding and breakthrough, while wettability mostly shifts that window rather than enlarging it.
method: Phase-field simulation of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes equations
Computed Laplace pressure curves for each geometry
Compared flat orifices, slits, diamond openings, and woven meshes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative gains: elongating a flat opening from aspect ratio 1 to 6 increases admissible pressure difference by 40% and stiffness by a factor of 3.3.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and geometry-specific, so real electrodes may differ due to manufacturing tolerances, pore connectivity, and surface heterogeneity.
paper_title: Phase-field simulation of interfacial stability in structured gas-liquid contactors: design rules for gas diffusion electrodes
